user_observation: Left arm swung sideways on Enable and then resisted manual movement as if tracking a pose.

findings.finding: Real Enable first arms joint-position control, holds, then requests hand-guiding; simulation Enable skips real motor-enable sequencing.
The policy callback starts only after successful service enable. The reported arm/leader exception occurred before that callback.
Leader method emits 0x151 01ff640000000200 then 0x470 fa00000000000000. These contain no joint-position, homing, motor-disable or explicit mounting-change command.

Official SDK says commands do not take effect while disabled. Production sends position seeds before enable; tests accept seeds while disabled. Firmware buffering and target-latching semantics are not established.
Mounting configuration records generic side mounting, not an independently measured left/right mounting setting.
Leader feedback packets demonstrate a protocol stream, not absence of stiffness or accurate gravity compensation.

Unintended position control during enable or leader transition fits sideways movement followed by stiff pose holding. Old targets, unsuccessful torque-mode transition and firmware behavior remain unresolved alternatives.
The incident directory has no raw CAN history, joint trajectory or deployed source snapshot; current source includes subsequent fixes.

next_required_evidence: Timestamped host TX and controller RX including mode, enable and position frames.
Joint angles through the enable/transition/error interval, paired with the observed motion.
Controller configuration and official firmware behavior for accepted targets and zero-force mode; exact mounting and tool/load setup.
